we have developed a parameter-optimized (PO) symplectic FDTD method that can be tailored to achieve a variety of dispersion characteristics.

the development and optimization of the symplectic FDTD method for electromagnetic wave propagation simulations.
the design of the PO-SFDTD method based on the (4.4) stencil, which can tailor the numerical dispersion error to meet different design specifications.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed PO-SFD method is a very powerful and flexible tool for simulating the electromagnetic wave propagation in dispersive media, especially when the dispersive characteristics are not known a priori.
the PO-SFDTD (4,4)-based method can be a good alternative for the conventional symplectic methods when the numerical dispersion behavior is not the main concern.
the proposed PO-SFD method is a good choice for the numerical modeling of electromagnetic problems, especially for those involving dispersive materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed PO-SFD method is an efficient tool for optimizing numerical dispersion and anisotropic properties of the conventional symplectic FDTD methods.
the proposed PO-SFD method can be used to tailor the numerical dispersive behavior of symplectic FDTD method to the desired specifications.
the PO-SFDTD method provides a general and flexible approach for optimizing the numerical dispersion behavior of symplectic FDTD methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the symplectic FDTD method is a promising approach to handle dispersion and anisotropic errors, which are the major obstacles for the practical implementation of higher-order methods in the electromagnetic field simulation.
the symplectic finite difference time domain method can be tailored to meet the requirements of different numerical applications.

the symplectic methods can be further optimized to tailor their numerical dispersion characteristics to the requirements of the application at hand, and the PO-SFDTD method is a good candidate for such applications.
